audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Logos prologue, life/light/darkness, John witness, Word embodied, grace/truth, Lamb of God, first disciples, Simon/Peter, Philip/Nathanael, Son of Humanity imagery.

verses.restored: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with the Divine, and the Word was Divine.

familiar.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

modern.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

original.text: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν, καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος.

verses.restored: This one was in the beginning with the Divine.

familiar.text: The same was in the beginning with God.

modern.text: He was with God in the beginning.

original.text: οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.

verses.restored: All things came into being through him, and apart from him not one thing came into being that has come into being.

familiar.text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

modern.text: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.

original.text: πάντα διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο οὐδὲ ἕν. ὃ γέγονεν

verses.restored: In him was life, and the life was the light of humans.

familiar.text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.

modern.text: In Him was life, and that life was the light of men.

original.text: ἐν αὐτῷ ζωὴ ἦν, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἦν τὸ φῶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων·

verses.restored: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome/comprehend it.

familiar.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

modern.text: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it. The Witness of John

original.text: καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει, καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν.

verses.restored: There came a human sent from the Divine; his name was John.

familiar.text: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.

modern.text: There came a man who was sent from God. His name was John.

original.text: Ἐγένετο ἄνθρωπος ἀπεσταλμένος παρὰ θεοῦ, ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἰωάννης·

verses.restored: This one came for witness, to bear witness concerning the light, so that all might trust through him.

familiar.text: The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.

modern.text: He came as a witness to testify about the Light, so that through him everyone might believe.

original.text: οὗτος ἦλθεν εἰς μαρτυρίαν, ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα πάντες πιστεύσωσιν διʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He was not the light, but came to bear witness concerning the light.

familiar.text: He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.

modern.text: He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light.

original.text: οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος τὸ φῶς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός.

verses.restored: The true light, which gives light to every human, was coming into the world.

familiar.text: That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.

modern.text: The true Light who gives light to every man was coming into the world.

original.text: ἦν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον.

verses.restored: He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, yet the world did not know him.

familiar.text: He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.

modern.text: He was in the world, and though the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him.

original.text: Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἦν, καὶ ὁ κόσμος διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ κόσμος αὐτὸν οὐκ ἔγνω.

verses.restored: He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.

familiar.text: He came unto his own, and his own received him not.

modern.text: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.

original.text: εἰς τὰ ἴδια ἦλθεν, καὶ οἱ ἴδιοι αὐτὸν οὐ παρέλαβον.

verses.restored: But as many as received him, to them he gave authority to become children of the Divine, to those trusting into his name,

familiar.text: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:

modern.text: But to all who did receive Him, to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God—

original.text: ὅσοι δὲ ἔλαβον αὐτόν, ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα θεοῦ γενέσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: who were born not from human lineage, nor from bodily impulse, nor from human will, but from the Divine.

familiar.text: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

modern.text: children born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God. The Word Became Flesh (Psalms 84:1–12)

original.text: οἳ οὐκ ἐξ αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος ἀνδρὸς ἀλλʼ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν.

verses.restored: And the Word became embodied life and pitched his tent among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of an only one from a father, full of grace and truth.

familiar.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

modern.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.

original.text: Καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας·

verses.restored: John bears witness concerning him and has cried out, saying, This was the one of whom I said, The one coming after me has come to be before me, because he was first of me.

familiar.text: John bare witness of him, and cried, saying, This was he of whom I spake, He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me.

modern.text: John testified concerning Him. He cried out, saying, “This is He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’”

original.text: (Ἰωάννης μαρτυρεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ κέκραγεν λέγων· Οὗτος ἦν ⸂ὃν εἶπον⸃· Ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·)

verses.restored: From his fullness we all received, and grace upon grace.

familiar.text: And of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace.

modern.text: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.

original.text: ⸀ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν, καὶ χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος·

verses.restored: For the Law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Messiah.

familiar.text: For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.

modern.text: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

original.text: ὅτι ὁ νόμος διὰ Μωϋσέως ἐδόθη, ἡ χάρις καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐγένετο.

verses.restored: No one has ever seen the Divine; the only Divine/Son, the one being in the bosom of the Father, that one has made him known.
verses.textual_note: Greek manuscript tradition varies between only-begotten God/only Divine and only-begotten Son.

familiar.text: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.

modern.text: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known. The Mission of John the Baptist (Isaiah 40:1–5; Matthew 3:1–12; Mark 1:1–8; Luke 3:1–20)

original.text: θεὸν οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε· ⸂μονογενὴς θεὸς⸃ ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο.

verses.restored: This is John's witness, when the Judeans sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, Who are you?

familiar.text: And this is the record of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, Who art thou?

modern.text: And this was John’s testimony when the Jews of Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, “Who are you?”

original.text: Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰωάννου ὅτε ⸀ἀπέστειλαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευίτας ἵνα ἐρωτήσωσιν αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ;

verses.restored: He confessed and did not deny; he confessed, I am not the Messiah.

familiar.text: And he confessed, and denied not; but confessed, I am not the Christ.

modern.text: He did not refuse to confess, but openly declared, “I am not the Christ.”

original.text: καὶ ὡμολόγησεν καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσατο, καὶ ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι ⸂Ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ⸃ ὁ χριστός.

verses.restored: They asked him, What then? Are you Elijah? He says, I am not. Are you the Prophet? He answered, No.

familiar.text: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elias? And he saith, I am not. Art thou that prophet? And he answered, No.

modern.text: “Then who are you?” they inquired. “Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”

original.text: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτόν· Τί οὖν; ⸂σὺ Ἠλίας εἶ⸃; καὶ λέγει· Οὐκ εἰμί. Ὁ προφήτης εἶ σύ; καὶ ἀπεκρίθη· Οὔ.

verses.restored: They said to him, Who are you, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?

familiar.text: Then said they unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?

modern.text: So they said to him, “Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”

original.text: εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ· Τίς εἶ; ἵνα ἀπόκρισιν δῶμεν τοῖς πέμψασιν ἡμᾶς· τί λέγεις περὶ σεαυτοῦ;

verses.restored: He said, I am a voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, just as Isaiah the prophet said.

familiar.text: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias.

modern.text: John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet: “I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way for the Lord.’”

original.text: ἔφη· Ἐγὼ φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Εὐθύνατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, καθὼς εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὁ προφήτης.

verses.restored: Those who had been sent were from the Pharisees.

familiar.text: And they which were sent were of the Pharisees.

modern.text: Then the Pharisees who had been sent

original.text: ⸀Καὶ ἀπεσταλμένοι ἦσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων.

verses.restored: They asked him and said to him, Why then do you baptize if you are not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?

familiar.text: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not that Christ, nor Elias, neither that prophet?

modern.text: asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”

original.text: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν βαπτίζεις εἰ σὺ οὐκ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ⸂οὐδὲ Ἠλίας οὐδὲ⸃ ὁ προφήτης;

verses.restored: John answered them, I baptize in water; among you stands one whom you do not know,

familiar.text: John answered them, saying, I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not;

modern.text: “I baptize with water,” John replied, “but among you stands One you do not know.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰωάννης λέγων· Ἐγὼ βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι· ⸀μέσος ὑμῶν ⸀ἕστηκεν ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε,

verses.restored: the one coming after me, of whom I am not worthy to loose the strap of his sandal.

familiar.text: He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe’s latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

modern.text: He is the One who comes after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”

original.text: ⸀ὁ ὀπίσω μου ⸀ἐρχόμενος, οὗ ⸂οὐκ εἰμὶ⸃ ἄξιος ἵνα λύσω αὐτοῦ τὸν ἱμάντα τοῦ ὑποδήματος.

verses.restored: These things happened in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

familiar.text: These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing.

modern.text: All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing. Jesus the Lamb of God (Matthew 3:13–17; Mark 1:9–11; Luke 3:21–22)

original.text: ταῦτα ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ὅπου ἦν ⸀ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων.

verses.restored: The next day he sees Jesus coming toward him and says, Look, the Lamb of the Divine, the one taking away the sin/misalignment of the world.

familiar.text: The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

modern.text: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!

original.text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον βλέπει τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ λέγει· Ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου.

verses.restored: This is the one about whom I said, After me comes a man who has come to be before me, because he was first of me.

familiar.text: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me.

modern.text: This is He of whom I said, ‘A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’

original.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ⸀ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον· Ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεται ἀνὴρ ὃς ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·

verses.restored: I myself did not know him, but so that he might be revealed to Israel, because of this I came baptizing in water.

familiar.text: And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.

modern.text: I myself did not know Him, but the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.”

original.text: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τῷ Ἰσραὴλ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον ἐγὼ ⸀ἐν ὕδατι βαπτίζων.

verses.restored: John bore witness, saying, I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove from heaven, and it remained upon him.

familiar.text: And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him.

modern.text: Then John testified, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.

original.text: καὶ ἐμαρτύρησεν Ἰωάννης λέγων ὅτι Τεθέαμαι τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ⸀ὡς περιστερὰν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν·

verses.restored: I myself did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize in water said to me, The one upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, this is the one baptizing in holy Spirit.

familiar.text: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said unto me, Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The man on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’

original.text: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν ἐν ὕδατι ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν· Ἐφʼ ὃν ἂν ἴδῃς τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπʼ αὐτόν, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ·

verses.restored: I have seen and have borne witness that this is the Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: And I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God.

modern.text: I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God. ” The First Disciples (Matthew 4:18–22; Mark 1:16–20; Luke 5:1–11)

original.text: κἀγὼ ἑώρακα, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκα ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ⸀ἐκλεκτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: The next day again John was standing with two of his disciples,

familiar.text: Again the next day after John stood, and two of his disciples;

modern.text: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.

original.text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον πάλιν εἱστήκει ⸀ὁ Ἰωάννης καὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο,

verses.restored: and looking at Jesus walking, he says, Look, the Lamb of the Divine.

familiar.text: And looking upon Jesus as he walked, he saith, Behold the Lamb of God!

modern.text: When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”

original.text: καὶ ἐμβλέψας τῷ Ἰησοῦ περιπατοῦντι λέγει· Ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: The two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus.

familiar.text: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.

modern.text: And when the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.

original.text: καὶ ἤκουσαν ⸂οἱ δύο μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ⸃ λαλοῦντος καὶ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Jesus turned and, seeing them following, says to them, What are you seeking? They said to him, Rabbi, which translated means Teacher, where do you remain?

familiar.text: Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? They said unto him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwellest thou?

modern.text: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”

original.text: στραφεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ζητεῖτε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί (ὃ λέγεται ⸀μεθερμηνευόμενον Διδάσκαλε), ποῦ μένεις;

verses.restored: He says to them, Come, and you will see. So they came and saw where he remained, and they remained with him that day; it was about the tenth hour.

familiar.text: He saith unto them, Come and see. They came and saw where he dwelt, and abode with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.

modern.text: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.

original.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔρχεσθε καὶ ⸂ὄψεσθε. ἦλθαν οὖν⸃ καὶ εἶδαν ποῦ μένει, καὶ παρʼ αὐτῷ ἔμειναν τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην· ὥρα ἦν ὡς δεκάτη.

verses.restored: Andrew, brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard from John and followed him.

familiar.text: One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

modern.text: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.

original.text: ἦν Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου εἷς ἐκ τῶν δύο τῶν ἀκουσάντων παρὰ Ἰωάννου καὶ ἀκολουθησάντων αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: He first finds his own brother Simon and says to him, We have found the Messiah, which is translated Anointed One.

familiar.text: He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.

modern.text: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).

original.text: εὑρίσκει οὗτος ⸀πρῶτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν ἴδιον Σίμωνα καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εὑρήκαμεν τὸν Μεσσίαν (ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον χριστός).

verses.restored: He brought him to Jesus. Looking at him, Jesus said, You are Simon son of John; you will be called Cephas, which is translated Peter/Rock.

familiar.text: And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.

modern.text: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter). Jesus Calls Philip and Nathanael

original.text: ⸀ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ Σίμων ὁ υἱὸς ⸀Ἰωάννου, σὺ κληθήσῃ Κηφᾶς (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος).

verses.restored: The next day he wanted to go out into Galilee, and he finds Philip. Jesus says to him, Follow me.

familiar.text: The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and findeth Philip, and saith unto him, Follow me.

modern.text: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”

original.text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ἠθέλησεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν. καὶ εὑρίσκει Φίλιππον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀκολούθει μοι.

verses.restored: Philip was from Bethsaida, from the city of Andrew and Peter.

familiar.text: Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.

modern.text: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.

original.text: ἦν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδά, ἐκ τῆς πόλεως Ἀνδρέου καὶ Πέτρου.

verses.restored: Philip finds Nathanael and says to him, We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, and the prophets: Jesus son of Joseph, from Nazareth.

familiar.text: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.

modern.text: Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets foretold—Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

original.text: εὑρίσκει Φίλιππος τὸν Ναθαναὴλ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὃν ἔγραψεν Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ καὶ οἱ προφῆται εὑρήκαμεν, ⸀Ἰησοῦν υἱὸν τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέτ.

verses.restored: Nathanael said to him, Can anything good be from Nazareth? Philip says to him, Come and see.

familiar.text: And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.

modern.text: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked. “Come and see,” said Philip.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Ἐκ Ναζαρὲτ δύναταί τι ἀγαθὸν εἶναι; λέγει αὐτῷ ⸀ὁ Φίλιππος· Ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.

verses.restored: Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and says concerning him, Look, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.

familiar.text: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

modern.text: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”

original.text: εἶδεν ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Ναθαναὴλ ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ· Ἴδε ἀληθῶς Ἰσραηλίτης ἐν ᾧ δόλος οὐκ ἔστιν.

verses.restored: Nathanael says to him, From where do you know me? Jesus answered and said to him, Before Philip called you, while you were under the fig tree, I saw you.

familiar.text: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.

modern.text: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Πόθεν με γινώσκεις; ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πρὸ τοῦ σε Φίλιππον φωνῆσαι ὄντα ὑπὸ τὴν συκῆν εἶδόν σε.

verses.restored: Nathanael answered him, Rabbi, you are the Son of the Divine; you are King of Israel.

familiar.text: Nathanael answered and saith unto him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.

modern.text: “Rabbi,” Nathanael answered, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ⸂αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ⸃· Ῥαββί, σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, σὺ ⸂βασιλεὺς εἶ⸃ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to him, Because I said to you, I saw you under the fig tree, do you trust? You will see greater things than these.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.

modern.text: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι εἶπόν σοι ⸀ὅτι εἶδόν σε ὑποκάτω τῆς συκῆς πιστεύεις; μείζω τούτων ⸀ὄψῃ.

verses.restored: He says to him, Amen, amen, I say to you: you will see heaven opened and the messengers of the Divine ascending and descending upon the Son of Humanity.

familiar.text: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.

modern.text: Then He declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, ὄψεσθε τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγότα καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
